clue.text: Smelling-salts make Sarah unpredictable

parts.note: Sal is a familiar short form of the name Sarah
volatile means liable to change suddenly and unpredictably

explanation.surface: Someone claims a bottle of restorative salts sends Sarah's moods all over the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' is only a link. Sal volatile is a solution of ammonium carbonate once sniffed to revive the faint.
explanation.definitionFit: Sal volatile is the old name for the aromatic ammonia solution used as a reviving restorative.

clue.text: Look forward to seeing a caroller?

parts.note: the waits were bands of street singers performing carols at Christmas, so one caroller is a wait

explanation.surface: Someone looks forward to the arrival of a carol singer at the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeing' is a link. In Britain 'waits' is an old word for groups of Christmas carol singers going door to door.
explanation.definitionFit: To expect something to come is to anticipate it, which is the same as looking forward to it.

clue.text: Futile to imprison sick criminal

indicators.note: imprisoning one word means locking it up inside another word, so the first holds the second

parts.note: a futile effort is a vain one
sick means ill

explanation.surface: It is pointless to lock up a criminal who is unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain is a wrongdoer or crook, a synonym for a lawbreaker.

clue.text: Inclined to get circular conservatory, maybe

parts.note: leant means sloped or inclined
the letter O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone is tempted to buy a round glass garden room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' joins the pieces; the surface tempts 'Inclined to' as one phrase. A lean-to is a shed or glasshouse built against a wall, so a conservatory may be one.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is an extension propped against a house wall, and a conservatory can be built that way.

clue.text: Mine host was once a composer

definitions.meaning: an old-fashioned jocular term for a pub landlord or innkeeper
John ... was a sixteenth-century English composer of church music

explanation.surface: The landlord of the pub used to write music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was once' covers both senses: an archaic word for an innkeeper, and the Tudor composer John Taverner.
explanation.definitionFit: An innkeeper is someone who keeps a tavern; John Taverner wrote masses in Tudor England.

clue.text: Design for which apprentice and I get no commission

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
taken as written
a cut is a share or commission taken from a deal

explanation.surface: A trainee complains that neither of them earns a percentage on the sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for which' and 'get' are links. L is the learner plate on a British car, hence apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: A linocut is a print made from a design carved into a block of linoleum.

clue.text: Two-horse race run on the level

definitions.meaning: an election contest between only two candidates
a contest conducted honestly, a fair bout

explanation.surface: A race with only two runners is held on flat ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'on the level' as honest and 'run' as a contest staged, rather than a race on flat ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest between just two candidates is a head-to-head; one conducted honestly is a fair fight.

clue.text: Dismiss cricketing Jack for getting a little motor

indicators.note: getting here means taking in or receiving, so the first word holds the second inside

parts.note: in cricket a batsman can be dismissed by being run out
jack and AB (able seaman) are both crossword sailors

explanation.surface: A batsman named Jack is run out in exchange for a small car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. Run out is a cricket dismissal where the batsman is caught short of the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: A runabout is a small, light car used for short trips.

clue.text: Managers seem disposed to accept many a complaint

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so the shuffled letters hold the next piece inside
disposed means arranged or set out, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword stand-in for many

explanation.surface: Bosses seem willing to put up with a great many grumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' looks like 'willing' in the surface but signals the anagram, giving GERMANMEASES; 'to accept' then takes in L. 'Complaint' is the illness sense, not a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: German measles is rubella, a mild viral illness, and complaint is an old word for an ailment.

clue.text: Fishermen may use it to seek suitable candidates

definitions.meaning: a wide dragnet towed behind a fishing boat
to search widely through many people for the right recruit

explanation.surface: A net used by fishermen is also used by recruiters looking for staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. The first reading is the net or the dragging of it; the second the figurative sweep of recruiters.
explanation.definitionFit: Boats drag a wide net along the sea; employers sweep through many applicants in the same spirit.

clue.text: Tavern due to be refurbished? It should be exciting!

indicators.note: refurbishing a building means doing it up anew, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A pub is due for a makeover, which promises to be thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be refurbished' rearranges TAVERN DUE. The definition is a description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventure is an exploit or escapade that by its nature ought to thrill.

clue.text: Do his classes prove a draw?

definitions.text: Do his classes prove a draw?

parts.words: Do his classes prove a draw?
parts.note: 'a draw' looks like something popular that pulls in a crowd, but here it is a sketch, the work of a teacher of drawing

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a particular teacher's lessons are popular.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher of drawing and painting has classes that produce pictures, which is a drawing.

clue.text: Beverage offered to marines by entrance

parts.note: cha (or char) is a slang word for tea
RM is the abbreviation for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A drink is handed to soldiers standing at the doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' is the verb, to enchant, not the doorway. 'offered to' and 'by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to enchant or captivate them, to cast a spell over them.

clue.text: Open-mouthed at joke about pious pole

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the first word goes round the others

parts.note: a gag is a joke
pi is informal for pious or sanctimonious
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: Someone is agape at a joke about a devout Pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link; 'pole' is the magnetic or geographic pole, not a Polish person.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaping means staring with the mouth wide open in surprise.

clue.text: Put pressure on craftsman of prejudiced views

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics
an artisan is a skilled manual worker

explanation.surface: Someone leans on a skilled tradesman who holds biased opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' and 'on' together signal that P is set in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan supporter is one-sided and biased in favour of a cause.

clue.text: Bargain successfully, but was subdued

definitions.meaning: to ... a seller is to haggle the price lower
the sense of being crushed or overcome, beaten into submission

explanation.surface: Someone haggled well but was left deflated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link. The phrasal verb works for knocking a price down in haggling, and for crushing resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggling a price lower is knocking a seller down; crushing someone is to quash or overpower them.

clue.text: About to drink gin? Rubbish!

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
to lap is to drink like a cat, with the tongue
a gin is a snare, so a trap

explanation.surface: Someone is about to have a glass of gin and dismisses an objection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link, and 'gin' is the snare rather than the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious nonsense, empty talk designed to win applause.

clue.text: Accelerator used with choke

definitions.meaning: the control that regulates fuel flow to an engine
to strangle someone by the throat

explanation.surface: A car's accelerator pedal is operated together with its choke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used with' is a link; the surface pairs two car controls, but 'choke' is the verb to strangle.
explanation.definitionFit: The pedal or valve that governs engine speed is the same word as to strangle.

clue.text: Tenor's in the mood to be a seducer

indicators.note: the word 'in' signals that the first piece sits inside the next

parts.note: temper means mood, as in a good temper
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A tenor feels in the mood to be a charmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be a' is a link, and the 's of 'Tenor's' is 'is', not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempter is someone who lures or entices another into wrongdoing.

clue.text: Hurry to find a heavy mallet

definitions.meaning: to ... along is to scurry or hurry
a heavy wooden hammer used for ramming or driving wedges

explanation.surface: Someone rushes off to fetch a big wooden hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to find' is a link. Both senses are less familiar than the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To scurry about is to beetle; a large wooden ramming hammer is also called a beetle.

clue.text: Passage from political pamphlet

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of or from, as in ex works
a tract is a short pamphlet arguing a political or religious case

explanation.surface: A passage is taken from a political leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a short excerpt quoted from a longer text.

clue.text: Carol points to burn-marks

parts.note: to carol is to sing
E and S are compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: A carol directs people to scorched marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; 'Carol' is the verb, not a name or noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Singes are slight surface burns, scorched marks.

clue.text: Peculiar term Diane found in offshore isle

indicators.note: being found in somewhere means being inside it, so the name goes within

parts.note: IOM is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea
Di is a short form of Diane

explanation.surface: An odd word used by Diane is heard on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peculiar' looks like an anagram signal but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is an expression peculiar to a language, whose meaning cannot be deduced from its words.

clue.text: Tip-off is of no avail

parts.note: a point is a tip, as of a pencil
off means less, as in ten pounds off the price

explanation.surface: A warning tip is no use at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip-off' reads as a warning but splits into two pieces; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pointless is futile, achieving nothing useful.

clue.text: Are returning to find poetic patroness

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word Are is read the other way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Coming back to find the woman who sponsors poets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns ARE into ERA; 'find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Muse of lyric and love poetry in Greek myth, a guiding spirit for poets.

clue.text: Rather entangled in embrace in front of the fire

indicators.note: the word 'in' signals one piece sitting inside the other

parts.note: a hug is an embrace

indicators.note: entangled means twisted up, so these letters are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: A couple are wrapped up in a cuddle by the fireside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entangled' shuffles the clue's 'Rather' to EARTHR and 'in' sets it within the cuddle. The definition is a place, standing in for the rug that lies there.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearthrug is a rug laid on the floor before a fireplace.

clue.text: Saw a daughter get on

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees
to get on is to grow older, to age

explanation.surface: Someone saw a daughter getting older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is the noun for a proverb, not the past tense of see.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, a traditional maxim.

clue.text: Suggestion that it's no job for an amateur

definitions.meaning: a proposal put forward for consideration
read whimsically as a post for a professional, a pro's position

explanation.surface: A proposal that only a professional should take on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that it's' links the two; the second reading splits into PRO and POSITION.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal put forward for discussion is a proposition; a professional's post splits the word the same way.
